aidb_assessment.novelty: The central contribution is a clean division-of-labor test: storage either adjudicates a contradiction or exposes it to an existing debate reasoner. The strongest novelty is experimental design and diagnosis rather than a new model architecture—independent mechanism switches, pre-declared gates, explicit reachability instrumentation, and publication of a correction that enlarges both positive and negative effects.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The controlled surface-versus-collapse comparison, paired uncertainty analysis, disclosure of the cap confound, and consequential negative results make the paper decision-relevant. However, a one-model evaluation, synthetic entity-level attacks, one judge, reduced temporal replication, and absence of genuine context overflow limit confidence in broad deployment claims. The work merits close reading and targeted internal replication before adoption.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High for designers of shared agent memory and retrieval evaluations. The evidence argues for retaining provenance-labelled alternatives until a reasoning component sees them, and for instrumenting whether an ablated mechanism actually fires. It also warns that topology-based write plausibility and provenance-heavy routing can be actively harmful. Direct production adoption should remain conditional because the evaluation is narrow and full context still wins on accuracy.

executive_summary: The paper tests whether shared memory should collapse contradictory facts before multi-agent debate or expose the ranked conflict set to agents. Its controlled ablation supports surfacing: in the reachable-conflict regime it substantially improves F1 and reduces successful poisoning at similar token cost. The initial protocol concealed much of the effect because its retrieval cap made most planted contradictions unreachable; the authors disclose and remeasure this confound. Write-time trust gating and router provenance features become harmful when conflicts are reachable. Evidence is unusually transparent, but generalization remains constrained by one model family, two corpora, synthetic attacks, a single judge, and memories that fit within the full context window.

assumptions: Only retrieved edges can form a conflict set; therefore mechanism exposure depends on retrieval reachability.
Corpus transcript facts are treated as ground truth and bypass write admission.
Single-valued relations define eligible contradictions; simultaneous assertions are treated as elaborations rather than conflicts.
The adversary can write and choose timestamps but cannot modify stored edges, inspect agent state, or alter prompts.
All agents in a round receive the same retrieved context, and one judge converts the debate into the scored answer.
The primary establishment rule is a paired bootstrap confidence interval excluding zero; subgroup analyses are pre-specified around poisoned and actually discriminating items.
key_components: A provenance-preserving edge representation with writer, validity interval, trust, source type, support, and links back to source episodes.
Four retrieval modes—vector, one-hop, multi-hop, and hybrid—behind a shared interface and a fixed prompt budget.
A write trust-gate based on groundedness, graph compatibility, relation compatibility, writer credibility, and a contradiction penalty.
A conflict resolver that detects distinct objects for a shared subject–relation key and compares collapse against surface.
DebateMem-Conflict, which injects later, type-consistent contradictory objects under a non-debating writer.
Pre-declared phase gates and single-mechanism ablations, followed by a disclosed retrieval-reachability correction.
method.overview: DebateGraph provides a common read/write/snapshot contract across four retrieval modes. Dialogue turns or document sentences become episodes; an LLM extracts provenance-linked triples into a bi-temporal store. At query time, vector, graph, or hybrid retrieval operates under a hard context budget. A resolver groups retrieved edges sharing a subject and relation but asserting distinct objects, ranks them by validity, trust, and cross-writer support, then either passes only the winner or the complete ranked conflict set. Each ablation changes one switch while downstream debate and judging remain fixed. Effects are evaluated with paired item-level comparisons, bootstrap confidence intervals, Wilcoxon tests, and exact McNemar tests for attack discordance.

open_questions: Does conflict surfacing outperform collapse with multiple independently served model families and multiple judge models?
Which surfaced fields—alternative claim text, writer identity, trust score, support count, or supersession state—cause the gain?
How does the mechanism behave when stored memory genuinely exceeds every available context window?
Can retrieval be optimized directly for conflict reachability without degrading ordinary evidence relevance or increasing prompt cost?
Does the result survive adaptive attacks involving paraphrases, coordinated writers, provenance spoofing, or several mutually supporting false edges?
Would a relative candidate-versus-incumbent admission rule avoid the trust-gate failure without suppressing truthful first mentions?

problem.importance: Premature reconciliation can erase useful disagreement and creates an attack surface when an adversarial writer controls the signal used for tie-breaking. The question is consequential because debate already supplies explicit reasoning machinery that could compare the claims.
problem.scope: The study concerns a multi-agent question-answering pipeline with shared episodic and graph memory, provenance-labelled contradiction injection, fixed-budget retrieval, three agents, two debate rounds, and one judge. It evaluates five switchable memory mechanisms across LoCoMo and a reduced HotpotQA document port under the stated write-adversary model.
problem.statement: Shared-memory systems commonly reconcile competing facts and return one winner before debate begins. The paper asks whether, with debate, budget, and retrieved evidence held fixed, storage should instead preserve a ranked set of contradictory claims and delegate adjudication to the agents.

proposed_experiments.baseline: For each of at least two additional independently served model families, compare collapse with surface using identical retrieved sets, prompts, budgets, attacks, and judges; include a judge-swap analysis.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Conflict surfacing improves paired answer quality and attack robustness across model families rather than only for the reported model.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired token-F1 difference on conflict-reachable items, with attack-success discordance as a co-primary safety endpoint and bootstrap confidence intervals reported per model.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop and reject model-independent generalization if the confidence interval includes zero for most added model families, if any adequately powered family shows a significant reversal, or if judge swaps change the direction.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Compare collapse, unlabelled competing claims, claims plus writer, claims plus support count, claims plus trust, claims plus supersession state, and the full surfaced representation under identical retrieval.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: The gain comes primarily from exposing competing claim content, while provenance annotations add smaller or inconsistent value.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired token-F1 on discriminating items, supplemented by prompt tokens and attack success rate.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop adding provenance fields when no field yields a confidence interval excluding zero over unlabelled competing claims, or when its accuracy gain is offset by a pre-declared token-cost threshold.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Construct long-memory partitions that necessarily overflow context; compare collapse and surface under matched retrieval, then repeat with template attacks, fluent paraphrases, coordinated multi-writer attacks, and provenance-spoofing attacks.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Surfacing remains beneficial when memory exceeds the model context window and under adaptive, fluent poisoning.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired token-F1 and attack success rate on items where both truthful and poisoned alternatives are demonstrably retrieved into the conflict set.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop and narrow the claim if surfacing fails to improve F1 with a confidence interval excluding zero in the overflow regime, or if any adaptive attack class eliminates the robustness benefit at matched cost.

artifacts: The paper states that code, per-query JSONL for all runs, the attack set, gate outputs, significance outputs, and corpus-validation outputs are released.
Every LLM call is cached on the full request payload for byte-identical replay.
Core corpora, attack construction, model, sampling parameters, budget, retrieval cap, agent and round counts, and paired statistical procedure are described.
Scripts are said to recompute tables and rebuild the harness and attack set deterministically.
reproducibility.assessment: Documentation and logged artifacts are unusually extensive, and full-payload caching should reproduce the reported executions closely. The rating remains partial because this review is restricted to the supplied text: the actual release cannot be inspected, no concrete artifact location appears, and exact environment and execution commands are not shown. Replaying cached outputs is strong result verification but is not equivalent to independently regenerating model behavior.
missing: The supplied document does not expose a concrete repository URL or artifact identifier, so availability cannot be independently checked from the provided material.
Exact runnable commands and a complete environment specification are not present in the supplied blocks.
The main model endpoint and local embedding hardware are described operationally but not with a fully portable infrastructure recipe.
The stochastic study uses cached calls; the supplied blocks do not demonstrate independent fresh-call replication across random seeds or alternative serving environments.

results.context: This is the strongest controlled comparison: collapse and surface use the same retrieval pipeline and prompt budget, while every poisonable item is attacked at the higher candidate-edge cap. It establishes both accuracy and attack-success endpoints in this regime.

evidence.quote: surfacing raises F1 from 0.116 to 0.456 (Δ=+0.340, CI [+0.267,+0.414], Wilcoxon p<10−4)
∗ denotes a 95% bootstrap CI excluding zero.
cuts attacks from 22 to 7 of 122
McNemar exact p=0.0003

results.result: In the reachable-conflict graph comparison, surfacing increased F1 from 0.116 to 0.456, a +0.340 change with 95% CI [+0.267,+0.414] and Wilcoxon p<10−4; successful attacks fell from 22 to 7 of 122, with exact McNemar p=0.0003.

results.context: This is both a validity threat and a useful diagnostic result. The cap ordered graph candidates without question relevance, so many identical prompts were tied by construction rather than demonstrating absence of treatment effect.

evidence.quote: Every conflict-dependent contrast, at the pre-declared cap of 40 and again at 200, same paired procedure.
surfacing, graph backend +0.043∗ +0.340∗ helps

results.result: The declared cap of 40 exposed only 12/51 poisoned items to a retrieved contradiction; reachability rose to 27/51 and 40/51 at larger caps. Accordingly, the graph surfacing contrast grew from +0.043 at cap 40 to +0.340 at cap 200.

results.context: The gate was intended to reject poisoned writes, but most measured action came from supersession invalidation. This makes the negative result mechanistically informative rather than merely a failed threshold.

evidence.quote: enabling the gate costs 0.075 F1 (CI [−0.133,−0.018], Wilcoxon p=0.039)
moves attacks the wrong way, 7→9 of 122.
it fires 123 invalidations against 3 rejections.

results.result: With contradictions reachable, enabling the write trust-gate cost 0.075 F1, with CI [−0.133,−0.018] and p=0.039, while attacks moved from 7 to 9 of 122. Its log showed 123 invalidations but only 3 rejections.

results.context: This supports directional cross-corpus replication only for the pre-specified subset where a conflict actually entered context. It does not establish a full-sample accuracy effect or an attack-success reduction.

results.result: On HotpotQA’s discriminating subset, surface minus collapse was +0.111 with CI [+0.010,+0.232], whereas the all-item effect was +0.032 with CI [-0.005,+0.077]. Attack success changed from 3 to 2 of 67 with McNemar p=1.00.

results.context: The proposed memory configuration does not beat the full-context accuracy ceiling. The graph deficit persists after relieving candidate truncation, suggesting that triple presentation—not only evidence coverage—limits performance in this setup.

evidence.quote: recall rises 0.30→0.76 while F1 moves 0.154→0.155

results.result: Full context achieved F1 0.503 on the multihop-temporal slice at 147,702 tokens per query, compared with vector retrieval at 0.304 and 6,405 tokens and graph retrieval at 0.154 and 11,199 tokens. Raising graph recall from 0.30 to 0.76 moved F1 only from 0.154 to 0.155.

title: Surfacing Disagreement Beats Resolving It: A Gated Ablation Study of Provenance-Weighted Memory for Multi-Agent Debate
